transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-10-08 15:00 PDT
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Location: Zoom
- Link: (recording) https://redwood.zoom/rec/ff-20251008-7a3b

Summary:
Quick kickoff for Silverbay Financial to align on security, network, and initial pilot sizing. Redwood team (AE + SE + CSM) + Silverbay platform, security, ML, procurement. Goals: confirm deployment mode (Private VPC vs Dedicated), network constraints, compliance requirements (SOC2/SSO/KMS), and next steps to start pilot in mid-October.

Topics (auto):
- Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
- Network connectivity & VPC peering
- SSO / SAML and RBAC mapping
- Data retention and audit logs
- Pilot sizing and success criteria

Action items (brief in call): see metadata action_items

Transcript body:
[00:00] Devon Hart: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Devon with Redwood, AE on the account. Quick intros?
[00:10] Alex Chen: Alex Chen, Head of Platform at Silverbay. We're leading the platform side; Priya is our security lead.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Hi all. Priya here, security.
[00:18] Marko Vukovic: Marko, ML eng. I'll own the benchmark and inference tests.
[00:22] Jasmin Ortega: Jasmin, procurement. I'll be tracking contracts.
[00:25] Sarah Lopez: Sarah, CSM, I'll run the onboarding plan and schedule.
[00:29] Maya Singh: Maya, SE, I'll take the deep dive on networking and runtime.

[00:35] Devon Hart: Cool. High level — we've been talking about a pilot for low-latency inference for your customer support summarization workflows. Today we want to lock down whether you need Private (VPC) or Dedicated pool, check network constraints, and agree on success metrics. 
[00:55] Alex Chen: Yeah, goal is to get something in staging that mirrors our prod infra. We have pretty locked down egress and firewall posture, so I suspect VPC peering or a Private install may be needed.
[01:10] Priya Nair: To be clear, SOC 2 and data residency are table stakes. Also we use our KMS for key management, want to ensure you can integrate with HSM or at least our cloud KMS.
[01:26] Maya Singh: Totally. Redwood private deployment supports customer-managed KMS; we can do KMS integration or bring-your-own HSM depending on your cloud. We'll share the runbook.
[01:36] Marko Vukovic: Performance question — if we go Private, will we still get the same throughput profiles as your hosted models? We push fairly high token throughput and want predictable p99 latency.
[01:50] Maya Singh: Good callout. The Dedicated pools give SLA-backed throughput. Private can be tuned to match — it's more dependent on reserved GPU types and kernel choices. For the pilot we recommend a small Dedicated overlay or a private cluster sized for your 95th percentile traffic; we'll provide recommended instance types and batch settings.
[02:12] Alex Chen: Is there a difference in how caching works — KV cache/prefix caching — between modes? We rely on cache to reduce costs.
[02:22] Maya Singh: Same caching primitives exist; with Private you have direct control over cache layer. Hosted has managed prefix caching and smart routing. Some customers prefer private to control cache retention windows and replicate caches across zones. There may be slight cost differences depending on memory sizing.
[02:40] Priya Nair: On encryption — we need to know what is encrypted at rest, audit log retention, and whether we can keep logs in our tenancy.
[02:48] Sarah Lopez: We can keep detailed audit logs; with Private we can push logs to your SIEM and control retention. We'll attach our audit log schema.
[02:58] Devon Hart: For procurement perspective Jasmin, any timeline constraints?
[03:02] Jasmin Ortega: Ideally pilot contract signed by Oct 20 to hit a November pilot window. We have internal vendor review that takes about a week once we have SOC 2 docs and SAML info.
[03:14] Devon Hart: OK. We'll aim to get SOC 2 and SAML docs by Friday.

[03:20] Maya Singh: Network specifics — Priya, can you confirm whether you allow inbound peering or only egress through NAT? Also whether TLS termination needs to be inside your VPC?
[03:33] Priya Nair: We prefer egress-only through a NAT gateway and strict egress allowlist; no inbound except peered private endpoints. TLS must terminate inside our boundary for certain sensitive traffic, but we can support mutual TLS if needed.
[03:47] Maya Singh: Makes sense. For VPC peering we can provide a private endpoint that your VPC routes to; if egress-only, we can also support a NAT egress pattern combined with strict IP allowlist. We'll include both patterns in the runbook.

[04:05] Marko Vukovic: For the benchmark — I want to test both quantized and fp16 variants. What's the process to onboard a model variant?
[04:16] Maya Singh: Simple. We'll pre-load the model variant in the pilot cluster; provide you a model alias for routing. We'll also help you run a small set of end-to-end prompts for latency/cost comparison. Expect a day of setup for each variant.
[04:30] Devon Hart: Success metrics — Alex, what are you measuring?
[04:33] Alex Chen: Two things: p95 latency under 500ms on our average 512-token prompt, and cost per 1k tokens under our threshold. Also stability — no unexpected fallbacks during business hours.
[04:45] Sarah Lopez: We'll draft a success criteria doc and include monitoring dashboards we can share in the Console.

[04:55] Jasmin Ortega: On procurement — any specific cancellation or data exposure clauses we should be aware of early on?
[05:01] Devon Hart: Our commercial team supports standard enterprise SLAs and data deletion commitments; we'll surface the contract redlines you typically ask for. For pilot we can do a statement of work.

[05:10] Priya Nair: One more security item — SSO mapping to RBAC. We use groups in Okta; we'd like to map Okta groups to Redwood roles.
[05:20] Maya Singh: We support SAML with group attribute mapping; we can demo role mapping and show how RBAC policies work in Console.

[05:30] Marko Vukovic: Are there any known gotchas with private deployments in our region (eu-west-1)?
[05:36] Maya Singh: We have private deployments in eu-west-1, but availability of specific GPU types can vary; we'll propose an instance family and fallbacks. Also region peering can add 20–40ms; we'll include region-aware routing options.

[05:53] Alex Chen: Okay, so next concrete steps?
[05:57] Sarah Lopez: I'll recap. Devon will send Dedicated pricing and pilot sizing sheet by Friday. Maya will post the VPC peering/NAT runbook and a network diagram template. I'll add Silverbay to our onboarding cohort and schedule the network walkthrough with Priya for Oct 13. Priya will share firewall/egress rules by Oct 9. Jasmin and Devon will coordinate procurement timeline.
[06:26] Devon Hart: Anything else before we wrap?
[06:28] Marko Vukovic: One small ask — can we get a sample prompt set for summarization so we can pre-populate tests?
[06:34] Maya Singh: Yes, we'll provide a starter prompt set and a script to run local load tests simulating token throughput.
[06:40] Alex Chen: Great. Thanks everyone.
[06:44] Devon Hart: Awesome, we'll follow up in email and share the items. Thanks all.
